blocks.text: BC Rental Pet Bans: What Pet Owners Need to Know in 2026

parts.t: If you've ever tried to find a rental in
with a dog or cat, you already know the drill — "no pets" is practically the default. That might be about to change.
— are calling on the provincial government to make good on a 2024 election promise and ban no-pet clauses in purpose-built rental buildings with five or more units.
The two organizations want the province to amend the

to prohibit landlords in larger rental buildings from refusing tenants based solely on pet ownership. The proposal targets buildings with five or more units — recognizing that a basement suite landlord operates very differently than a purpose-built rental tower.

, the NDP included a specific pledge: "ending the bias against pet owners by getting rid of no pet clauses in purpose-built rental apartment buildings." As of April 2026, that promise hasn't been acted on — but advocacy is ramping up.
The argument for keeping pets out has always been about damage. First United reviewed actual
decisions on pet-related disputes going back eight years.
, the pet damage was fully covered by the pet deposit already permitted under the RTA. The average portion retained by landlords for repairs was just over 71%.
Since 2014, the BC SPCA has taken in more than
whose owners were struggling with housing — and that's only what was reported to the SPCA.

Pet bans hit some groups harder than others. First United has documented cases where the inability to find pet-friendly housing contributed to displacement and homelessness — particularly for women escaping violence, seniors, and people in the 2SLGBTQAI+ community. Service dog owners have also reported being turned away despite legal protections.

For landlords, there's also a financial argument. As First United put it: "For a landlord that owns a large building, or even a few units, it's illogical to forego hundreds of thousands of dollars in rental revenue based on speculations about pet damage."

blocks.text: Where Things Stand in BC (vs. Other Provinces)

parts.t: Ontario banned no-pet clauses in rental agreements almost 30 years ago. BC hasn't gone that far yet. Under BC's
, landlords and tenants can negotiate the pet question — but landlords can still refuse entirely.
Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs

said the province is "exploring options for pet policies in purpose-built rental buildings." No timeline given. In 2020, Vancouver City Council passed a motion calling for an end to no-pet restrictions. The
and the provincial Select Standing Committee on Finance and Government Services made similar calls in 2023.

blocks.text: What This Means for the South Surrey & White Rock Market

parts.t: If pet-friendly rental restrictions are loosened, you'd likely see stronger rental demand in buildings that currently ban pets. That could put upward pressure on rents and may push some renters who've been forced to buy just to house their pet back into the rental market.
— keep in mind this proposal targets purpose-built rentals, not stratas. Strata pet bylaws are governed separately under the
. If you're buying into a strata that restricts pets, that bylaw doesn't go away under this proposal.
